raised.claim: Guard-3-degraded matcher_bug verdicts are pushed into `quiet` and then counted as `wontfix` in the daily digest line, because the quiet loop treats every non-not_on_untappd quiet verdict as wontfix.
raised.why_it_breaks: When a not_on_untappd verdict is degraded to matcher_bug (no probe ran), planTriageActions pushes it into `quiet`. The job's quiet loop increments `outcome.wontfix` for it, so `buildTriageLine` reports e.g. "3 wontfix" for rows that are actually matcher_bug enrich-retry rows — the digest understates wontfix and hides the degradation.

raised.claim: `covered` is computed from the raw analysis verdicts, not from verdicts that actually survived the guards, so a run where the guards skipped every verdict still logs covered === batch and the guardHits line never fires.
raised.why_it_breaks: Model returns a verdict for each of 50 orphans, all routed to a saturated/unscoped issue. plan.skipped = 50, guardHits.saturated = 50, but covered = 50 = orphans.length, so the shortfall warn (the only place guardHits is logged) is not emitted. The 'one line of visibility' the design rests on is silently absent in exactly the loop-the-model-keeps-making case it was built for.

raised.quote:
review_class       = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.review_class END,
       review_note        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.review_note END,
       reviewed_at        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.reviewed_at END
raised.claim: recordEnrichFailure's re-open path clears review_class/review_note/reviewed_at when candidates_count crosses the 0↔>0 boundary but leaves `issue_number` pointing at the old issue, so countRowsForIssue keeps counting a re-opened, untriaged row toward that issue's saturation count.
raised.why_it_breaks: Row is triaged matcher_bug → #347 (issue_number=347). Later the beer re-fails with candidates_count crossing 0→>0; review_class is reset to NULL (row re-enters the untriaged pool) but issue_number stays 347. countRowsForIssue(347, ...) still counts it, permanently inflating postCreationRows toward MAX_ROWS_PER_ISSUE=12; after enough re-opens the issue is falsely saturated and refuses all new attachments.

raised.claim: parseScopeBlock takes the FIRST ```triage-scope fence in the issue body, and a new issue's body is model-authored prose appended before the job-rendered block — so a fence the model writes inside `body` shadows the trusted rendered scope on the next run.
raised.why_it_breaks: The model submits new_issues with a legal structured `scope`, but its free-text `body` also contains a ```triage-scope block with different content (e.g. {"beer_ids":[],"where":[{"col":"review_class",...}]}). The job appends renderScopeBlock after the body; next run parseScopeBlock returns the model's fence, not the rendered one, so guard 2 enforces a scope the structured field never declared — the 'we parse our own output, not model prose' invariant is broken whenever the model emits a fence in body.

raised.quote:
export const V23_BACKFILL_SQL = `
  UPDATE enrich_failures
     SET issue_number = CAST(substr(review_note, instr(review_note, '→ #') + 3) AS INTEGER)
   WHERE review_note LIKE '%→ #%'
raised.claim: The v23 backfill only matches the unicode arrow '→ #'; the code comment in the same file describes the legacy suffix as ASCII '-> #123', so notes written with the ASCII form are silently not backfilled.
raised.why_it_breaks: If any of the 198 legacy rows carry 'alias -> #347' (ASCII hyphen-gt, as the migration comment itself writes the format), LIKE '%→ #%' is false, issue_number stays NULL, and those rows are invisible to countRowsForIssue — the saturation guard undercounts exactly the historical magnet issues (#347, #254) the guard exists to constrain. Confidence is low only because the actual note corpus is not shown; the comment/SQL inconsistency is in the diff itself.

raised.quote:
`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM enrich_failures
        WHERE issue_number = ? AND reviewed_at > ?`
raised.claim: countRowsForIssue compares reviewed_at (always stored via toISOString(), with '.000' millis) to GitHub's created_at (typically '…T00:00:00Z', no millis) as raw strings, so a row reviewed in the same second the issue was created compares as reviewed_at < created_at and is dropped from the count.
raised.why_it_breaks: Issue created_at = '2026-08-14T12:00:00Z'; a verdict written in that same second has reviewed_at = '2026-08-14T12:00:00.000Z'. Lexicographically '.' < 'Z', so the row is excluded by `reviewed_at > ?` even though it was attached at/after creation. Off-by-one undercount of postCreationRows; low practical impact given the 12-row threshold, but the comparison is not a correct instant comparison.
